look_here_first: First inspect alternate leaves (often coarsely toothed but occasionally entire) and narrow cylindrical flower heads. Use a loupe to check 18–22 phyllaries in 5–6 overlapping series and 13–20 disk florets. At fruiting, confirm mostly hairless cypselae with 30–35 tawny pappus bristles. Do not use river-gravel habitat or leaf teeth alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Branched woody shrub about 60–120 cm; stems finely hairy and sparsely gland-dotted.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, short-petiolate (1–2 mm); blades lanceolate to lance-ovate, 5–40 × 3.5–12 mm, faintly three-veined from base; margins usually coarsely toothed but sometimes entire; gland dots.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Narrow panicle of cylindrical to bell-shaped involucres 7–11 mm, phyllaries 18–22 in 5–6 series, florets 13–20, pale green/yellow tubular disk corollas.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Cypselae 3.5–4 mm, usually glabrous; 30–35 tawny barbellate to subplumose pappus bristles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Mostly hairless mature cypselae with tawny bristles
